An engine-wide weighted limiter caps admitted segment backing arrays at 256 MiB and three buffers, covering HLS VOD/live/WebVTT, DASH initialization/fragments, and segmented merge/refresh. It reserves before body reads, rounds unknown-length ranges for possible MemoryStream growth, limits range reads to the requested length, shrinks from reliable Content-Length and actual capacity, and returns backing slices instead of making a second full copy for binary media. AES-128 retains a two-copy reservation through validation and writing. This is a segment-buffer budget, not a process working-set cap: pooled read chunks, parser/crypto scratch, playlist/key metadata and assembled subtitle cues sit outside it. Per-object size remains capped at 64 MiB; streaming AES, larger parts and measured peak-memory comparisons remain open.
